# Muhammad Ahmad Naeem

> Muhammad Ahmad Naeem is a production and manufacturing engineer in Sydney, Australia. He works on beverage and food plants across PET bottle, carton and can lines: production, maintenance, reliability, loss reduction and plant data.

## Facts

- What does he do? He is a production and manufacturing engineer who works on the plant floor of beverage and food factories. His work covers production, maintenance, reliability, loss reduction and plant data.
- Where is he based? Sydney, New South Wales, Australia.
- Which lines has he worked on? PET bottle lines, Tetra Pak carton lines for juice, and can lines, across carbonated soft drinks, juice and water, plus a noodle plant at Unilever.
- Which equipment does he know? KRONES, SIDEL and Tetra Pak equipment: blow moulders, mixers, fillers, cappers, labellers, packers, conveyors and water treatment.
- What has he delivered? Eleven water conservation projects saving 306,000 cubic metres a year, a nitrogen dosing rebuild that cut nitrogen use by 40 percent, commissioning of a SIDEL blow moulder and a reverse osmosis plant, and PKR 61 million in verified savings at PepsiCo.
- Where has he worked? Refresco Australia, Elgas, PepsiCo, OneScreen and Unilever.
- What is his education? BSc in Mechanical Engineering from GIK Institute (2024), and a Master of Professional Engineering (Mechanical) in progress at the University of Technology Sydney.
- How do I contact him? Email m.ahmad.naeem5@gmail.com, phone +61 408 158 938, or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/m-ahmad-naeem-

## Selected projects

- Eleven water conservation projects (PepsiCo): Mapped where a three line beverage plant used its water, then fixed the largest losses first: reverse osmosis reject reuse, rinser water recovery, closed loop cooling and pressure settings by pack size. Result: 306,000 m³ of water saved every year.
- Nitrogen dosing rebuilt as pulse dosing (PepsiCo): The dosing unit on a water line had been dead for years and nitrogen ran by hand. Rebuilt it with a solenoid mechanism and sensor triggered, PLC controlled pulses tuned per bottle size. Result: 40% less nitrogen used, about PKR 20 million a year.
- New SIDEL blow moulder and reverse osmosis plant (PepsiCo): Commissioned a new SIDEL blow moulding machine on a PET line and a new reverse osmosis water treatment plant, from installation through to stable production. Result: 2 new assets handed over to production.
- Main bearing change on a KRONES rotary filler (PepsiCo): Abnormal vibration pointed to the filler main bearing. Planned the shutdown, opened the carousel, replaced the bearing and rebuilt with alignment checks before restart. Result: 20% approximate OEE gain across his time on the lines.
- Automated handling for LPG cylinder cages (Elgas): A simple mechanical concept chosen over a robotic cell so it works with the existing cages and daily operations, with the door opening mechanism and retainer designed in CAD. Result: < 1 yr estimated payback in the business case.
- Reliability and maintenance dashboard (Refresco Australia): A Power BI dashboard that brings live line data and SAP maintenance data together, so downtime, breakdowns and efficiency are read from one place. Result: Live published and used across the site.
- Material yield model for syrup, caps and preforms (Refresco Australia): A model built on SAP stock counts that shows material loss per process order, per day, per product and as a monthly trend. Result: 3 materials tracked from order level to monthly trend.
- Automatic lubrication on a food plant (Unilever): Replaced manual lubrication rounds with automatic lubrication on critical equipment at a 13 line noodle plant. Result: 40% fewer equipment failures.

## Writing

- [Rebuilding a dead nitrogen doser into pulse dosing](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/nitrogen-dosing-rebuilt-as-pulse-dosing.html): How a nitrogen dosing unit on a bottled water line was rebuilt with sensor triggered, PLC controlled pulses and cut nitrogen use by about 40 percent.
- [Replacing the main bearing on a rotary filler](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/replacing-the-main-bearing-on-a-rotary-filler.html): How abnormal vibration on a KRONES rotary filler was treated as a reliability job, from diagnosis to a planned main bearing change.
- [My first six days on any plant](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/my-first-six-days-on-any-plant.html): The plant manual I build in the first week on a new site, and why clarity comes before tools.
- [Where the water goes in a beverage plant, and where to look first](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/water-in-a-beverage-plant.html): The order I follow to find water savings on a beverage plant, from eleven projects that save 306,000 cubic metres a year.
- [How to measure syrup, cap and preform yield on a bottling line](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/measuring-material-yield-on-a-bottling-line.html): The choices that make a material yield model work on a PET line, starting with stock counts instead of goods issues.
- [Tilted caps, a vibrating capper and the restart I refused to rush](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/tilted-caps-and-the-restart-i-refused-to-rush.html): A capping fault on a PET line that turned out to have more than one cause, and why the restart had to wait.
- [Designing automation for LPG cylinder cages](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/designing-automation-for-lpg-cylinder-cages.html): What an industry project with Elgas taught me about designing automation for a real operating site.
- [How a PET bottling line works, from preform to pallet](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/how-a-pet-bottling-line-works.html): A plain walk through a PET soft drink line, machine by machine, and where these lines usually lose time.
- [What OEE hides on a beverage line](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/what-oee-hides-on-a-beverage-line.html): OEE is one number built from three, and on a filling line the detail underneath matters more than the headline.
- [From GIK to a Sydney plant floor](https://ahmadnaeempbc.github.io/from-gik-to-a-sydney-plant-floor.html): How a mechanical engineering graduate from Pakistan ended up back beside fillers and blow moulders on the other side of the world.
